pm_exper_user_4197_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: Any tips for working on detailed model projects for long stretches without feeling sore afterward?
pm_exper_user_4197_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Since you’ve dealt with a wrist tendon strain from earlier model-making, it helps to set up your work so tools and pieces sit at a comfortable height, and to switch between fine detail and broader tasks every 20–30 minutes. Using ergonomic grips or lighter tools can take pressure off your wrist, and a brief stretch break will keep you comfortable over long sessions.
(b) It’s a good idea to keep your workspace comfortable, with tools and materials within easy reach, and to take short breaks every so often while working. Switching between tasks and stretching occasionally can help prevent stiffness after long hours on a project.
(c) Given your history with wrist strain from detailed modeling work, and your architect’s eye for precision, you might adjust your drafting table to keep your wrist in a neutral position and switch between tools to vary your grip. Pair that with short breaks to gently stretch and a comfortable pair of formal shoes to support your posture during longer standing sessions.
(d) Because you’ve had a tendon strain in your wrist from intensive past modeling, it’s worth keeping your workspace adjusted to reduce strain—placing work at elbow height and alternating between sitting and standing. Choosing lightweight, well-balanced tools and pausing for a minute of gentle stretches can make a huge difference over a long day.

- Invite her input on areas she can influence, such as finding efficiencies or contributing to proposals.
